heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Ghana
heroData.subtitle: Hire in Accra Without an Entity
heroData.description: Our Ghana Employer of Record solution enables you to hire full-time employees without establishing a local subsidiary. We handle SSNIT contributions, GRA tax filings, and labor compliance under Act 651.

steps.title: Employee Classification
steps.description: We verify the employee's role and salary to ensure compliance with the Ghana Labour Act 2003 (Act 651). For expatriates, we assess quota availability under GIPC regulations.

steps.title: Contract Generation
steps.description: Issuance of a compliant employment contract. Contracts must specify hours of work (max 40 hours/week), overtime rates, and termination notice periods.

steps.title: Statutory Registration (SSNIT & GRA)
steps.description: Registration of the employee with the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) and the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) for Tax Identification Number (TIN/Ghana Card).

steps.title: Payroll Setup
steps.description: Configuration of monthly salary payments, including Tier 1 and Tier 2 pension deductions and PAYE tax calculations.

steps.title: Induction & Handover
steps.description: Employee receives the handbook and undergoes safety induction. Onboarding is typically completed within 2 weeks.

rows.label: Tiers 1 & 2 Pension (Employer)
values: 13% to SSNIT, 5% to Private Scheme. Total 18% employer burden.

rows.label: Setup Fee
values: One-time fee for contract and registration.

items.title: Immigrant Quota System
items.text: Foreign nationals cannot be hired freely on EOR. The EOR partner must hold available 'immigrant quotas' tied to their GIPC capital, or apply for specific work permits.

items.title: 13th Month Salary
items.text: While not statutory under Act 651, a 13th-month bonus is a strong market norm in Ghana and expected by skilled professionals.

items.title: Termination Rules
items.text: Termination requires 'fair grounds' (capacity, conduct, or redundancy). Redundancy triggers severance pay negotiation, often guided by industry Collective Agreements.

faqs.question: Can EORs sponsor work permits?
faqs.answer: Yes, but strictly limited by their 'Immigrant Quota'. An EOR with $500k capital typically has a quota of 2-3 expats. Check availability before hiring non-Ghanaians.

faqs.question: Is probation mandatory?
faqs.answer: Probation is common but not mandatory. If used, it typically lasts 3 to 6 months and must be specified in the employment contract.

faqs.question: What is the notice period?
faqs.answer: For contracts of 3+ years, one month's notice or pay in lieu is required. For less than 3 years, 2 weeks' notice applies.

steps.title: Data Aggregation
steps.description: Collection of timesheets, variable pay (commissions, bonuses), and deduction updates by the 20th of the month.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Processing salary with 5.5% SSNIT deduction (Tier 1 & 2) to determine 'Taxable Pay'. Application of PAYE tax table on Taxable Pay.

steps.title: Employer Contributions
steps.description: Adding Employer SSNIT (13%) to the cost. Note: Maximum insurable earnings are capped at ~61,000 GHS.

steps.title: Disbursement
steps.description: Net pay transfer to employee bank accounts (Ecobank, GCB, Stanbic, etc.) by the 25th-30th. Cash payments discouraged.

steps.title: Statutory Filing
steps.description: Submission of PAYE returns to GRA and SSNIT contributions by the 14th of the following month.

items.title: Tier 1: Basic Social Security
items.text: Managed by SSNIT. Mandatory. Employer pays 13%, Employee pays 0% (from the 18.5% total, 13.5% goes to SSNIT, rest to Tier 2).

items.title: Tier 2: Occupational Pension
items.text: Mandatory privately managed scheme. 5% contribution. Usually, the 18.5% total SSNIT is split: 13.5% to SSNIT, 5% to Tier 2.

items.title: Tier 3: Provident Fund
items.text: Voluntary. Up to 16.5% of basic salary can be contributed tax-free by the employee or employer.

rows.label: Union Dues
values: Applicable if Collective Bargaining Agreement exists.

faqs.question: What is the overtime rate?
faqs.answer: Overtime is generally 1.5x hourly rate for weekdays and 2.0x for weekends/public holidays, though this can vary by Collective Agreement.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, bonuses are taxable. However, bonuses up to 15% of annual basic salary are taxed at a concessional rate of 5%. Amounts above this are added to total income and taxed at marginal rates.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late SSNIT payment?
faqs.answer: A penalty of 3% per month on the unpaid contribution amount.

items.title: Tax Reliefs
items.text: Reliefs are available for marriage, child education, and old age, but must be applied for. The calculator shows standard PAYE.

items.title: Allowances
items.text: Cash allowances are generally fully taxable. Car and accommodation elements are taxed based on statutory values.

items.title: Bonuses
items.text: Remember the 5% tax rate applies only to bonuses up to 15% of annual basic salary.

faqs.question: Is transport allowance taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, unless it is a reimbursement for actual business costs (receipted), it is treated as income.

faqs.question: How is 13th month taxed?
faqs.answer: It is taxed as a bonus. The first 15% of annual basic is at 5%, the rest at marginal rates.

faqs.question: Do expats pay SSNIT?
faqs.answer: Expats are required to contribute to SSNIT unless they can prove they are contributing to a state pension in their home country (rarely exempted).

heroData.title: Incorporation in Ghana
heroData.subtitle: Set Up Your Business with ORC
heroData.description: Establish your legal entity in Ghana through the Office of the Registrar of Companies (ORC). We navigate the Companies Act 2019 (Act 992) and GIPC registration for you.

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Search and reserve your company name at the RGD/ORC. Fee is ~50-100 GHS. Approved names are valid for 30 days.

steps.title: TIN & Ghana Card
steps.description: Directors and shareholders must have a Tax Identification Number (TIN). The Ghana Card PIN is now used as the TIN for individuals.

steps.title: Forms 3 & 4
steps.description: Complete the 'Returns of Particulars' (Form 3) and 'Constitution' (Form 4). These detail the directors, secretary, auditor, and shares.

steps.title: Payment & Submission
steps.description: Pay the registration fee (approx 450 GHS) and Stamp Duty (0.5% of stated capital). Capital stamp duty is critical.

steps.title: Certificate & Commencement
steps.description: Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate to Commence Business. Act 992 merged these in practice, but 'Commencement' is still a key milestone.

steps.title: GIPC Registration
steps.description: Foreign-owned companies must register with the Ghana Investment Promotion Centre (GIPC) after incorporation. Minimum capital rules apply.

steps.title: Capital Verification
steps.description: Transfer the required minimum capital ($500k for 100% foreign owned) to a Bank of Ghana approved account. Obtain Bank Confirmation Letter.

steps.title: Application
steps.description: Submit GIPC specific forms along with ORC certificates and proof of capital transfer.

steps.title: Fee Payment
steps.description: Pay the GIPC annual registration fee (approx 31,500 GHS as of latest schedule).

steps.title: Certification
steps.description: Receive the GIPC Certificate, which grants benefits like immigrant quotas and profit repatriation rights.

rows.label: Joint Venture (Foreign + Ghanaian)
values: Ghanaian partner must hold at least 10% equity.

rows.label: Trading Enterprise (Foreign)
values: Retail/Trading. Also requires hiring 20 skilled Ghanaians.

rows.label: Export Enterprise
values: No minimum capital for purely export-oriented firms.

items.title: Company Secretary
items.text: Under Act 992, appointing a qualified Company Secretary is mandatory for all companies. They must be a lawyer, CA, or professional administrator.

items.title: Beneficial Ownership
items.text: You must disclose the Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) holding 10%+ interest. This information is entered into the Central Register.

items.title: Stamp Duty
items.text: Stamp duty is 0.5% of stated capital. Keep initial stated capital reasonable to minimize costs, unless GIPC limits require otherwise.

faqs.question: Can I own 100% of my company?
faqs.answer: Yes, 100% foreign ownership is permitted in most sectors, provided you meet the $500,000 capital requirement.

faqs.question: How long does it take?
faqs.answer: RGD incorporation takes 5-10 business days. GIPC registration can take an additional 2-4 weeks.

faqs.question: Do I need a local director?
faqs.answer: Act 992 requires at least one director to be 'ordinarily resident' in Ghana. If all directors are foreign, you may need a resident nominee or manager.

heroData.title: Staffing in Ghana
heroData.subtitle: Recruit Top Talent in West Africa
heroData.description: Access Ghana's growing talent pool in tech, finance, and mining. We handle recruitment, vetting, and work permit processing for expat staff.

steps.title: Quota Verification
steps.description: Check if the company has an available GIPC quota. Quotas are auto-granted based on investment ($50k-$250k: 1 quota, $500k: 2 quotas, etc.).

steps.title: Document Verification
steps.description: Applicant provides CV, Police Report, Medical Report, and Educational Certificates. Copies must be notarized.

steps.title: GIS Application
steps.description: Submission of application to Ghana Immigration Service (GIS). Fee is ~$1000 for Non-ECOWAS nationals.

steps.title: Non-Citizen Card
steps.description: Applicant must register for a Non-Citizen Identity Card (FIMS) from the National Identification Authority. Cost: $120.

steps.title: Approval
steps.description: Permit is usually issued for 1 year, renewable. Processing time: 2-4 weeks with expedite.

items.title: Tech Hub of West Africa
items.text: Accra is a major tech hub with institutions like MEST training high-quality software developers. Competition for senior devs is high.

items.title: Background Checks
items.text: Standard reference checks are essential. Academic fraud can occur, so verify degrees directly with universities.

items.title: ECOWAS Free Movement
items.text: Citizens of ECOWAS states (e.g., Nigeria, Cote d'Ivoire) do not need visas to enter, but still require a residence/work permit for long-term employment (process is cheaper/faster).

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors in Ghana?
faqs.answer: Yes, but be careful of misclassification. If they work set hours and use your equipment, they may be deemed employees by the Labour Commission.

faqs.question: What is the typical severance pay?
faqs.answer: Severance is not fixed by law but is 'negotiable'. A common standard is 1-3 months' salary per year of service.

faqs.question: Are internships paid?
faqs.answer: Internships are regulated as 'apprenticeships' or 'casual work'. While not strictly mandated to be high paying, transportation stipends are expected.

heroData.title: HRIS in Ghana
heroData.subtitle: Digital HR Management
heroData.description: Modernize your workforce management with HRIS solutions tailored for Ghana's tax laws and banking interfaces.

rows.label: BambooHR
values: Excellent UI, requires manual tax setup

rows.label: Setup & Migration
values: Depends on employee count and data history.

rows.label: Training
values: On-site or virtual training for HR admins.

steps.title: GRA & SSNIT Reports
steps.description: System must generate the specific monthly CSV/Exl files required by GRA and SSNIT portals.

steps.title: Tier 3 Management
steps.description: Ability to handle voluntary Provident Fund deductions and track varying percentages.

steps.title: Loan Management
steps.description: Many Ghanaian employees take salary advances or loans. The HRIS should track repayment schedules automatically.

items.title: Data Hosting
items.text: Under the Data Protection Act, ensure your HRIS provider complies with data sovereignty rules if personal data is stored offshore.

items.title: Mobile First
items.text: Choose an HRIS with a strong mobile app. Smartphone penetration is high, and employees prefer accessing payslips/leave via phone.

faqs.question: Do local banks integrate with HRIS?
faqs.answer: Yes, many local HRIS (like Hubtel or expressPay components) integrate directly with mobile money and bank transfers for one-click salary payments.

faqs.question: Is cloud HRIS accepted by GRA?
faqs.answer: GRA accepts digital records, provided they can be audited. Cloud hosting is fine, provided Data Protection rules are met.

faqs.question: How long does implementation take?
faqs.answer: For a company of 50-100 employees, typical implementation (data migration + training) takes 4-6 weeks.

heroData.title: Accounting in Ghana
heroData.subtitle: IFRS Compliant Bookkeeping
heroData.description: Ensure financial compliance with Ghana's CIT, VAT, and levies. We provide bookkeeping, audit support, and annual return filing.

rows.label: NHIL & GETFund
values: Charged on value of supply (Effective VAT ~21.9%)

steps.title: Auditor Appointment
steps.description: Appoint a licensed CA at the AGM. Notify the Registrar of Companies.

steps.title: Interim Audit
steps.description: Preliminary review of internal controls and systems (usually mid-year).

steps.title: Final Fieldwork
steps.description: Detailed testing of balances, verification of assets, and stock counts at year-end.

steps.title: Financial Statements
steps.description: Drafting FS in accordance with IFRS. Board approval required.

steps.title: Signing & Filing
steps.description: Auditor signs the opinion. Accounts are filed with the ORC (Annual Return) and GRA (Tax Return).

items.title: IFRS Adoption
items.text: Ghana fully adopted IFRS in 2007. All companies must prepare accounts per IFRS (or IFRS for SMEs). ICAG is the regulator.

items.title: E-Invoicing (E-VAT)
items.text: GRA is rolling out electronic VAT invoicing. Large taxpayers must integrate their ERPs with the GRA API for real-time invoicing.

items.title: Audit Requirement
items.text: All companies, regardless of size, must have their accounts audited annually by a qualified Chartered Accountant.

faqs.question: What is the financial year?
faqs.answer: The standard financial year is January 1 to December 31. Changing it requires GRA approval.

faqs.question: Are losses carry-forward allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, losses can generally be carried forward for 3 to 5 years depending on the industry (Priority sectors get 5 years).

faqs.question: Is Transfer Pricing regulated?
faqs.answer: Yes, strictly regulated under TP Regulations 2020. Documentation is required for related party transactions over certain thresholds.

steps.title: Annual Returns (ORC)
steps.description: File Form 3 with the Registrar of Companies. Penalty is 1000 GHS/month for delay.

steps.title: Renew GIPC Certification
steps.description: Renew GIPC registration every 2 years for foreign entities.

steps.title: Data Protection Renewal
steps.description: Renew registration with Data Protection Commission (DPC) every 2 years.

steps.title: Business Operating Permit
steps.description: Pay annual fee to the local Metropolitan/Municipal Assembly (AMA, TMA, etc.).

steps.title: Online Application
steps.description: Create an account on the Data Protection Commission (DPC) website.

steps.title: Questionnaire
steps.description: Complete the form detailing nature of data processed (Employee, Customer, Biometric, etc.).

steps.title: Data Supervisor
steps.description: Appoint and register a certified Data Protection Supervisor (DPO).

steps.title: Payment & Certificate
steps.description: Pay the fee (tiered by revenue/size) and receive the certificate.

items.title: Mandatory Registration
items.text: All entities processing personal data must register. The public database discloses compliant companies.

items.title: Data Sovereignty
items.text: Sensitive data should usually be stored locally. Cross-border transfer requires DPC approval or proof of adequate protection (e.g., GDPR compliance).

faqs.question: What are the penalties for late Annual Returns?
faqs.answer: Since May 2024, the penalty is 1000 GHS per month of default. Persistent default can lead to company strike-off.

faqs.question: Do I need a local Safety Certificate?
faqs.answer: Yes, a Fire Certificate from Ghana National Fire Service is required for physical offices.

faqs.question: Who is liable for non-compliance?
faqs.answer: Directors and Officers of the company can be held personally liable for certain statutory breaches, especially tax and social security.

rows.label: CST (Comm Service Tax)
values: Telcos and ISPs charge this to consumers.

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Register with GRA via the Taxpayers Portal using Ghana Card/TIN.

steps.title: Monthly Returns
steps.description: File PAYE, WHT, and VAT returns by the 15th/end of the month.

steps.title: Quarterly CIT
steps.description: Pay estimated Corporate Income Tax in quarterly installments.

steps.title: Annual Return
steps.description: File final CIT return within 4 months of year-end (usually by April 30).

items.title: Tax Clearance Certificate (TCC)
items.text: A TCC is required for many business activities, including government tenders, renewing permits, and clearing goods at ports.

items.title: Exemptions
items.text: Free Zone companies enjoy 10 years tax holiday. Manufacturing in regional capitals offers reduced CIT rates.

items.title: Tax Amnesty
items.text: GRA occasionally offers waivers on penalties for voluntary disclosure. Keep an eye on annual budget statements.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for tax evasion?
faqs.answer: Evasion can lead to fines of up to 300% of the tax due and potential imprisonment under the Revenue Administration Act.

faqs.question: Does Ghana have Double Tax Treaties?
faqs.answer: Yes, with countries like UK, France, Germany, South Africa, etc., which can reduce withholding tax rates.

faqs.question: Is VAT refundable?
faqs.answer: Yes, input VAT can be claimed against output VAT. Excess credits can be refunded, though the process can be lengthy.

heroData.title: MSA & Legal in Ghana
heroData.subtitle: Corporate Law & M&A
heroData.description: Expert legal guidance for Mergers, Acquisitions, and complex Master Service Agreements in Ghana.

items.title: SEC Approval
items.text: For public companies, relevant mergers require Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approval under the Takeover Code.

items.title: Sector Approvals
items.text: Bank of Ghana (Banking), National Insurance Commission (Insurance), and NCA (Telecoms) must approve M&A in their sectors.

items.title: Act 992
items.text: The Companies Act 2019 introduced statutory mergers, allowing two companies to merge into one entity (Amalgamation) without liquidation.

steps.title: Due Diligence
steps.description: Legal and Financial DD covering tax liabilities, pending litigation, and title to assets (land is a key risk area in Ghana).

steps.title: Share Purchase Agreement
steps.description: Drafting the SPA. Ensure choice of law is Ghana or a neutral venue like London (Arbitration).

steps.title: Regulatory Notification
steps.description: Notify ORC and sector regulators. Competition notification may be needed if thresholds are met.

steps.title: Closing & Tax
steps.description: Pay Stamp Duty. Capital Gains Tax (15%) applies to the seller.

faqs.question: Is arbitration binding?
faqs.answer: Yes, Ghana is a signatory to the New York Convention. Foreign arbitral awards are enforceable.

faqs.question: Can we use English law?
faqs.answer: Yes, contracts can be governed by Foreign law, but employment and local property matters will almost always be subject to Ghanaian law.

faqs.question: Are electronic signatures valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the Electronic Transactions Act 2008, digital signatures are generally recognized.

items.title: Commercial Courts
items.text: Ghana has dedicated Commercial Courts designed for faster resolution of business disputes.

items.title: Mediation
items.text: Pre-trial mediation is often mandatory in Commercial Court proceedings to encourage settlement.

heroData.title: Software Solutions in Ghana
heroData.subtitle: West Africa's Innovation Hub
heroData.description: Diverse software development landscape ranging from Fintech to Agrotech. Tap into the 'Silicon Accra' ecosystem.

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.description: Post on LinkedIn, Ghana Tech Lab, or contact MEST Africa for alumni.

steps.title: Technical Assessment
steps.description: Remote testing is common. HackerRank or take-home projects. Verify GitHub availability.

steps.title: Equipment
steps.description: Provide high-spec laptops (MacBooks are preferred but expensive locally). Consider importing.

steps.title: Remote Setup
steps.description: Clarify internet allowance. Data is relatively expensive in Ghana; offering a subsidy is standard.

items.title: MEST Africa
items.text: The Meltwater Entrepreneurial School of Technology (MEST) is a major incubator, producing high-caliber startups and talent.

items.title: Google AI Center
items.text: Accra hosts Google's first AI research center in Africa, elevating the local AI/ML talent pool.

items.title: Accra Digital Center
items.text: A government-backed BPO and Tech park providing infrastructure for tech companies.

faqs.question: Is internet reliable for remote work?
faqs.answer: Yes, in major cities (Accra, Kumasi) fiber and 4G/5G are reliable. Starlink is also becoming an option.

faqs.question: What is the preferred tech stack?
faqs.answer: JavaScript/TypeScript (React, Node) is very dominant. Python and PHP (Laravel) are also widely used.

faqs.question: Are there good co-working spaces?
faqs.answer: Yes, Impact Hub, Kawa Moka, and Carbon offer world-class facilities for remote teams.

heroData.title: Marketing in Ghana
heroData.subtitle: Digital & Traditional Reach
heroData.description: Connect with the Ghanaian consumer through top-tier agencies specializing in social media, influencers, and experiential marketing.

steps.title: Briefing
steps.description: Define target audience (Urban vs Rural) and KPIs. Language is key (English vs Twi/Ga ads).

steps.title: Platform Selection
steps.description: Choose mix. Tik Tok is huge for youth. Facebook is dominant for mass market. Twitter/X for corporate/news.

steps.title: Production
steps.description: Create assets. Video content performs best. ensure local context usage.

steps.title: Execution
steps.description: Launch ads. Monitor cost-per-click (CPC) which is relatively low in Ghana compared to global avg.

items.title: Influencer Marketing
items.text: Ghana has a vibrant influencer scene (Twitter/X and TikTok). Micro-influencers often deliver better ROI for niche products.

items.title: Radio is King
items.text: Despite digital growth, Radio remains the most effective medium for mass market reach in Ghana.

items.title: Cultural Sensitivity
items.text: Respect traditional values and authorities (Chiefs) in ad messaging to avoid backlash.

faqs.question: What is the best platform for B2B?
faqs.answer: LinkedIn is growing but Twitter/X is surprisingly effective for B2B conversations in Ghana.

faqs.question: How expensive is TV advertising?
faqs.answer: Prime time slots on major channels (TV3, Joy Prime) can cost GHS 5,000 - 10,000 per 30s spot.

faqs.question: Are giveaways effective?
faqs.answer: Highly. 'Momo' (Mobile Money) giveaways are the fastest way to drive engagement.
